title: Grateful Dead Live at Baltimore Civic Center on 1973-03-26
lineage: Dat (Sony R500) -> SEK'D Prodif Plus -> Samplitude Profesional v8.01 -> FLAC

ai_review.summary: A crystal‑clear Miller soundboard transfer captures a monster March 26 1973 Baltimore show, highlighted by the legendary Truckin’ → Weather Report Suite jam and an unstoppable second set.
ai_review.review: The Miller‑sourced stereo recording is praised as crisp, hi‑fi and virtually flawless, delivering every nuance of what many reviewers call a “monster” performance.  The band rides a soaring first set into a second‑set masterpiece – Truckin’ spilling into the Weather Report Suite Prelude, Wharf Rat, Eyes → Morning Dew and a blistering Here Comes Sunshine – with tight interplay and inspired solos throughout.  Minor comments note a slightly uneven first half, but overall the show is deemed one of the finest spring‑1973 outings.

ai_rating.rationale: Over two dozen enthusiastic reviews (mostly 5‑star) celebrate both the superb Miller soundboard transfer and an exceptional performance, with only minimal criticism of the first set.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Stereo hi‑fi Miller transfer praised as crisp, clear and well‑balanced; no reported dropouts or major flaws.

standout_songs: Truckin' > Weather Report Suite Prelude > Wharf Rat
China Cat Sunflower > I Know You Rider
show_quality.setlist_flow: First set solid with a few uneven moments, but the second set is a seamless, high‑energy suite of jams and transitions that many reviewers call flawless.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Garcia’s tone described as clean, passionate and “cooking” on solos (Here Comes Sunshine, Truckin'), delivering soaring leads throughout.
band_member_comments.Phil: Lesh praised for powerful ending notes on Morning Dew, high‑note work in Eyes, and a sweet groove in China Cat Sunflower.
band_member_comments.Keys: Keith Hartman noted as “on big time,” providing strong backing and tasteful fills that lift the second‑set jams.
band_member_comments.Drums: Bill Kreutzmann’s single‑drummer groove highlighted as tight, driving and essential to the show’s momentum.
